command:
set -eo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
cd /tmp
URL=https://s3.amazonaws.com/giab/data/NA12878/PacBio_SequelII_CCS_11kb/HG001_GRCh38/HG001_GRCh38.haplotag.RTG.trio.bam
echo "== pull chr20 PacBio HiFi reads back to FASTQ =="
# -F 0x900 drops secondary and supplementary records, so each read appears exactly once.
# Going back to FASTQ is the point: minimap2 must do a real alignment, not inherit pbmm2's.
samtools view -b -F 0x900 -@ 4 "$URL" chr20 > chr20.bam
samtools fastq -@ 4 -n chr20.bam | gzip -1 > hifi.chr20.fq.gz
NREADS=$(( $(zcat hifi.chr20.fq.gz | wc -l) / 4 ))
BASES=$(zcat hifi.chr20.fq.gz | awk 'NR%4==2{n+=length($0)} END{printf "%.0f", n}')
MEANLEN=$(awk -v b="$BASES" -v r="$NREADS" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", b/r}')
BYTES=$(stat -c%s hifi.chr20.fq.gz)
DEPTH=$(awk -v b="$BASES" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b/64444167}')
{
  echo "reads             $NREADS"
  echo "bases             $BASES  (awk %d would clamp this to INT32_MAX)"
  echo "mean_read_len     $MEANLEN  want 8000..20000 (library size-selected ~9-11 kb)"
  echo "depth_on_chr20    ${DEPTH}x  want >=20 (the deposit is ~30x genome-wide)"
  echo "fastq_bytes       $BYTES"
} > prep-check.txt
cat prep-check.txt
test "$NREADS" -gt 50000
test "$MEANLEN" -ge 8000
test "$MEANLEN" -le 20000
awk -v d="$DEPTH" 'BEGIN{exit !(d>=20)}'
echo 'PREP CHECK PASSED'
